mbpp_0635.reference_description: Write a function to push all values into a heap and then pop off the smallest values one at a time.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to push all values into a heap and then pop off the smallest values one at a time.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinHeap and HeapSort Implementation in JavaScript

Main goal of the code:
- Implement a min-heap data structure with push, pop, and size operations, including internal sift-up and sift-down procedures to maintain the heap property.
- Provide a heapSort function that uses the min-heap to sort an iterable in ascending order by inserting all elements into the heap and then repeatedly popping the minimum.

What the code does:
- MinHeap class:
  - push(value): adds a value to the heap and reorders to maintain min-heap property using _siftUp.
  - pop(): removes and returns the smallest element (root). Replaces it with the last element and reorders using _siftDown.
  - size(): returns the number of elements in the heap.
  - _siftUp(): moves the last inserted element up the tree until the parent is smaller or equal.
  - _siftDown(): moves the root element down to its correct position by swapping with the smaller of its children when needed.
- heapSort(iterable):
  - Creates a MinHeap and pushes all elements from the iterable into it.
  - Repeatedly pops the minimum element to produce a sorted array in ascending order, and returns that array.

Notes:
- The implementation keeps the heap as an array with standard binary-heap indexing.
- If the input is empty, heapSort returns an empty array.

mbpp_0408.reference_description: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Purpose and Functionality of the MinHeap and kSmallestPairs

Main goal of the code:
- Implement a min-heap data structure and use it to efficiently find the k smallest sum pairs from two sorted arrays.

What the code does:
- MinHeap class:
  - Stores elements in an array-based binary heap.
  - push(val): inserts a value and restores the heap property by sifting up.
  - pop(): removes and returns the smallest element (top) and restores the heap property by sifting down.
  - size(): returns the number of elements in the heap.
  - _siftUp(): internal method to move the last element up until the heap property is satisfied. Assumes elements are comparable by their first item (element[0]).
  - _siftDown(): internal method to move the root down to maintain the min-heap property, comparing based on element[0].

- kSmallestPairs(nums1, nums2, k):
  - Uses the MinHeap to generate the k smallest sum pairs from two arrays nums1 and nums2 (assumed sorted in non-decreasing order).
  - push(i, j): helper that pushes a candidate triplet [sum, i, j] onto the heap, if indices are in range.
  - Initialization: push(0, 0) to start with the smallest possible sum.
  - Main loop: repeatedly pop the smallest-sum pair, add [nums1[i], nums2[j]] to the result.
  - After popping, it explores the next pair in two directions to enumerate potential next smallest sums:
    - push(i, j + 1) (move in nums2)
    - if j === 0, also push(i + 1, 0) (move in nums1 when starting a new row)
  - Continues until k pairs are collected or the heap becomes empty.

Notes:
- The algorithm relies on nums1 and nums2 being sorted to ensure the k smallest sums are discovered in order.
- The heap stores elements as [sum, i, j] and compares by sum (element[0]).

Overall: The code provides a min-heap implementation and uses it to efficiently compute the k smallest pairs by sum from two sorted arrays.

mbpp_0031.reference_description: Write a function to find the top k integers that occur most frequently from given arrays of sorted and distinct integers using heap queue algorithm.

Title: Finding the Top-k Frequent Elements across a 2D Array

Main goal:
- Compute the frequency of each number appearing in any sub-array of nums.
- Return the k elements that have the highest frequencies (ties resolved by usual heap behavior).

What the code does:
- Builds a frequency map d by iterating through all rows and their elements, counting occurrences of each number.
- Defines a MinHeap class that stores pairs [frequency, value] and keeps the smallest frequency at the top.
- Iterates over the frequency map:
  - If the heap has fewer than k elements, pushes [frequency, value].
  - Otherwise, if a value’s frequency is greater than the smallest frequency in the heap, replaces the smallest with [frequency, value].
- Extracts elements from the heap (in ascending order of frequency due to min-heap) and returns the corresponding values, giving the k most frequent elements from the input.

Notes:
- The result array is built by repeatedly popping from the heap, so it will be in ascending order of frequency; the code returns the k most frequent values but not necessarily in any specific order.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the nth super ugly number from a given prime array of size k using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Min-Heap Based Generator for nth Super Ugly Number

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the nth "super ugly number" given a list of prime factors, using a custom min-heap to efficiently merge multiples.

What the code does:
- Defines a MinHeap class implementing a min-heap with push, pop, and internal up/down heapify operations.
- Implements nthSuperUglyNumber(n, primes):
  - Initializes uglies with [1].
  - Builds a MinHeap containing an entry for each prime: {val: prime, prime, idx: 0}.
  - Repeatedly pops the smallest value from the heap, appends it to the uglies sequence if it’s not a duplicate of the last value, and pushes a new node representing the next multiple of that prime: {val: prime * uglies[node.idx + 1], prime, idx: node.idx + 1}.
  - Stops when the nth ugly number is reached and returns it.

High-level behavior:
- Uses a priority-queue (min-heap) to merge multiples of given primes with the list of already found ugly numbers, avoiding duplicates, to generate the sequence of super ugly numbers in increasing order.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the first missing positive number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Missing Positive Integer Finder (In-Place)

Summary_description:
This JavaScript function computes the smallest missing positive integer in an array using O(1) extra space (in-place). It first checks if 1 is present; if not, returns 1. It then replaces non-positive or out-of-range values (> n or <= 0) with 1. Next, it uses a marking trick by adding n to positions corresponding to values (arr[i] - 1), encoding presence. Finally, it scans for the first index i where arr[i] was not marked (arr[i] <= n) and returns i + 1 as the missing positive; if all positions are marked, it returns n + 1. This effectively finds the smallest positive integer not present in the array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Common Subsequence of Three Strings (3D DP)

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the length of the longest common subsequence among three strings X, Y, and Z.

What it does:
- Initializes a 3D dynamic programming table L of size (m+1) x (n+1) x (o+1), filled with zeros.
- Iterates through all indices i, j, k representing prefixes of X, Y, and Z.
- If any index is 0, L[i][j][k] = 0 (base case).
- If the current characters X[i-1], Y[j-1], Z[k-1] are all equal, it increments the L[i-1][j-1][k-1] value by 1.
- Otherwise, it takes the maximum value from removing one character from any of the three strings: L[i-1][j][k], L[i][j-1][k], or L[i][j][k-1].
- Returns L[m][n][o], which is the length of the longest common subsequence of X, Y, and Z.

mbpp_0223.reference_description: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Code Purpose — Check if a value is a Majority in a Sorted Array

Main goal of the code:
- Determine whether a given value x appears as a true majority in the first n elements of a sorted array arr. A majority means x occurs at least floor(n/2) + 1 times within the subarray arr[0..n-1].

What the functions do:
- binarySearch(arr, low, high, x)
  - Performs a modified binary search to find one occurrence of x in the sorted array segment between low and high.
  - It targets the first occurrence where the element equals x (by checking that either mid is 0 or x is greater than the previous element, and arr[mid] === x). If found, returns the index; otherwise recurses left or right or returns -1 if not present.

- isMajority(arr, n, x)
  - Calls binarySearch to locate an occurrence of x in arr[0..n-1].
  - If x is not found, returns false.
  - If found at index i, it checks whether the element at index i + floor(n/2) is also x (i.e., there are at least floor(n/2) elements after i that equal x within the subarray). If that condition holds, returns true; otherwise returns false.

In short, it uses binary search to locate x and then verifies that there are enough consecutive x's after the found position to constitute a majority within the first n elements.

Title: GCD-based count of common divisors

Main goal: This code computes the number of positive common divisors of two integers x and y by first finding their greatest common divisor (gcd) and then counting the divisors of that gcd.

Functions:
- ngcd(x, y): Brute-force gcd calculation by checking all integers from 1 up to min(x, y) and updating gcd when they divide both numbers.
- num_comm_div(x, y): Uses ngcd to get n = gcd(x, y), then counts the divisors of n efficiently by iterating up to sqrt(n). For each divisor i of n, it adds 2 to the count (for i and n/i), with a correction when i equals n/i to avoid double-counting. Returns the total number of common divisors of x and y.

Title: Spiral Matrix Generator

Main goal: The function generateMatrix(n) creates an n x n matrix filled with the integers from 1 to n^2 arranged in a clockwise spiral pattern starting from the top-left corner and moving rightward.

What it does:
- Validates n > 0; returns an empty array for non-positive n.
- Initializes an n-by-n matrix filled with zeros.
- Maintains four boundaries (rowSt, rowEd, colSt, colEd) and a current value starting at 1.
- Repeatedly fills:
  - the top row from left to right within current boundaries,
  - the rightmost column from top to bottom,
  - the bottom row from right to left,
  - the leftmost column from bottom to top,
  while shrinking the boundaries inward after each edge.
- Increments the current value with each cell assigned until reaching n^2, then returns the completed spiral matrix.

The function isSamePatterns(colors, patterns) checks if the colors correspond to a consistent one-to-one mapping with patterns. It first ensures the arrays have the same length. Then, for each list of colors associated with a given pattern, it verifies that all colors in that list are identical. If any pattern is associated with different colors, it returns false. Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Smallest Common Multiple Finder Using Adapted Step Increment

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of a given n, using a custom incremental search strategy.

What the code does:
- If n <= 2, returns n immediately.
- Initializes i to 2n and builds a list of “factors” by collecting numbers from n down to 2 that satisfy number*2 > n (i.e., numbers greater than n/2 up to n).
- Enters an infinite loop that checks each candidate i against all values in factors:
  - If i is not divisible by any factor a, i is incremented by n and the inner loop restarts.
  - If i is divisible by all factors (reaches the last factor without triggering a skip), it returns i as the result.
- In effect, it searches for the least common multiple of the set of factors, using steps of size n, instead of directly computing the LCM. The resulting i is the smallest multiple of n that is divisible by every element in the factors list.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Multiphase Stock Trading Profit Maximization

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the maximum profit achievable with at most k stock transactions (buy-sell pairs) given an array of daily prices.

What the code does:
- price is an array of daily stock prices.
- n is the number of days.
- finalProfit[i][j] stores the maximum profit using at most i transactions within the first (j+1) days.
- Initialization: with 0 transactions or on day 0, profit is 0.
- For each transaction count i from 1 to k, and for each day j from 1 to n-1:
  - It considers the best single-day buy-sell ending on day j by scanning all previous days x < j and computing
    currPrice = price[j] - price[x] + finalProfit[i-1][x]
    which represents completing the i-th transaction by buying on day x and selling on day j, on top of the best (i-1) transactions up to day x.
  - maxSoFar tracks the best such value ending on day j.
  - finalProfit[i][j] is the maximum of either not transacting on day j (finalProfit[i][j-1]) or the best transacted value ending on j (maxSoFar).
- The function returns finalProfit[k][n-1], i.e., the maximum profit using at most k transactions over the full period.

Goal: The code counts how many hexadecimal digits in the integer range [L, R] are letters (A-F, i.e., digits 10–15) when each number is represented in base-16.

How it works:
- Iterate through each integer i from L to R.

In short: counts all hexadecimal digits in the range [L, R] that are alphabetic hex digits (A–F) in their base-16 representation.

mbpp_0689.reference_description: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block

Description_Simple.reference_text: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming solution to minimum jumps in an array

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the minimum number of jumps required to reach the last index of the array, where each element arr[i] represents the maximum jump length from that position. If the end is unreachable, it returns Infinity.

What the code does:
- Initializes an array jumps of length n to store the minimum jumps needed to reach each index; jumps[i] is the minimum jumps to reach index i.
- If the array length n is 0 or the first element arr[0] is 0 (cannot move), it returns Infinity (unreachable).
- Sets jumps[0] = 0 since you are already at the first index with zero jumps.
- Iterates i from 1 to n-1, initializing jumps[i] to Infinity.
- For each i, iterates j from 0 to i-1 and checks if index i is reachable from j (i <= j + arr[j]) and if index j was itself reachable (jumps[j] !== Infinity). If so, it updates jumps[i] to the smaller of its current value and jumps[j] + 1, and breaks out of the inner loop (choosing the first viable predecessor).
- After filling the array, it returns jumps[n - 1], the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index; if unreachable, this will be Infinity.

Notes:
- This is a dynamic programming approach with O(n^2) time and O(n) extra space.
- The early break in the inner loop means it picks the first qualifying predecessor, which still yields the minimum in this particular implementation due to the iteration order.

mbpp_0971.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming to Maximize Segments

Summary_description:
This function computes the maximum number of segments into which a total length n can be cut, using segment lengths a, b, or c. It uses a 1D DP array where dp[i] stores the maximum number of pieces to reach length i (initialized with -1 except dp[0] = 0). For each reachable length i, it tries to extend by a, b, or c (if within bounds) and updates dp[i+length] with the best (largest) piece count. The result is dp[n], i.e., the maximum number of segments that sum exactly to n, or -1 if not possible.

mbpp_0256.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.

mbpp_0468.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product formed by multiplying numbers of an increasing subsequence of that array.

mbpp_0918.reference_description: Write a function to count coin change.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count coin change.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Coin Change Count using Dynamic Programming

Summary_description:
This function computes the number of ways to make change for a target sum n using m coin denominations provided in array S. It builds a 2D DP table where rows represent values from 0 to n and columns represent using the first j+1 coin types. The value table[i][j] counts ways to make sum i with coins up to index j. Base case sets table[0][i] = 1 (one way to make sum 0). Recurrence: x is the number of ways to make i using coin S[j] (i - S[j], same j), and y is the number of ways to make i without using coin S[j] (same i, previous column j-1). The final result returns table[n][m-1], i.e., the number of ways to make sum n using all m coin types.

mbpp_0751.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given array represents min heap or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given array represents min heap or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Min-Heap Validation Function

Main goal of the code:
- To recursively verify whether a given array represents a valid min-heap, where each parent node is less than or equal to its children.

What the function does:
- checkMinHeap(arr, i = 0) checks the heap property starting from index i (default root at 0).
- If the node at index i has no left child (2*i + 2 > arr.length), it’s a leaf or beyond, and returns true.
- It computes:
  - leftChild: arr[i] <= arr[2*i + 1] and recurses on the left child index (2*i + 1).
  - rightChild: either there is no right child (2*i + 2 === arr.length) or arr[i] <= arr[2*i + 2] and recurses on the right child index (2*i + 2).
- Returns true only if both leftChild and rightChild conditions hold, ensuring the min-heap property for the current node and recursively for its subtrees.

mbpp_0702.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Removals to Satisfy Max Gap Constraint

Main goal of the code:
- Given an array and a value k, determine the minimum number of elements to remove so that, after removing, the remaining elements can be arranged (implicitly sorted) so that the difference between the largest and smallest elements within any kept subsequence of consecutive elements does not exceed k. The code achieves this by sorting the array and then for each element arr[i], finding the farthest index j such that arr[j] - arr[i] <= k, and computing the number of removals needed as n - (j - i + 1). The minimum over all i is returned.

Key functions:
- find_ind(key, i, n, k, arr): For a given starting index i, it performs a binary search to find the furthest index ind > i where arr[ind] - key <= k. Returns -1 if no such index exists.
- removals(arr, n, k): Sorts the array ascending, iterates over each index i, uses find_ind to locate the farthest j with arr[j] - arr[i] <= k, and updates the minimum removals as n - (j - i + 1). Returns the minimal removals needed.

mbpp_0622.reference_description: Write a function to find the median of two sorted arrays of same size.

It tracks the last two values (m1, m2) seen while advancing pointers i and j through arr1 and arr2, and stops after processing n+1 elements. The result is the average of m1 and m2, which yields the median of the combined 2n elements.

mbpp_0448.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.

Title: JavaScript Function to Compute a Specific Sum Sequence

Summary_description:
The function calSum(n) computes a running sum of a sequence defined by an initial triple (a, b, c) = (3, 0, 2). For n = 0, 1, or 2 it returns fixed values (3, 3, and 5 respectively). For n > 2 it initializes sum to 5 and iteratively generates a new term d = a + b, adds d to sum, then updates (a, b, c) ← (b, c, d) and decrements n until n <= 2. The result is the cumulative sum of the sequence terms up to the (n)-th step, effectively producing a specific Fibonacci-like sequence (with a, b, c as a rolling window) and summing its generated terms.

mbpp_0181.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Obfuscated JS string/array decryption and common prefix utility

Main goal of the code:
- This code defines several obfuscated helper functions that decrypt and cache strings, then perform a common-prefix computation between arrays of strings. It includes two main decryption utilities (_0x452e and _0x1c35) that decode base64-like payloads with a customized RC4-like step and memoize results to avoid recomputation. It also defines commonPrefixUtil and commonPrefix functions to compute the longest common prefix across elements of string arrays, using the decryption helpers to access obfuscated data.

Key components and their roles:
- _0x452e and _0x1c35: Primary decryption/decoder functions.
  - Each takes a pair (_0x163b92, _0xfcfdd2) and decodes an obfuscated string from an internal array (fetched via _0x197f()) with a caching layer. They initialize their own decryption routines once (tLHqFs / xnHkKe) and store results in gdggPH / MyszZf caches.
  - They rely on a hidden array of strings returned by _0x197f() and use a small offset to pick an entry, then decode it.

- Internal decryption routines:
  - _0x439ba6 inside both functions decodes base64-like input using a custom alphabet and then percent-escapes to produce a decoded string.
  - _0x53259e inside _0x1c35 is a XOR-based/RC4-like stream cipher that further decodes an already-decrypted string with a key.

- commonPrefixUtil:
  - Given two arrays/strings, it computes the common prefix by iterating character-by-character until a mismatch, returning the matched prefix.

- commonPrefix:
  - Given an array of strings (_0x4dd00f) and a count (_0x353aa8), it reduces to the longest common prefix by repeatedly applying commonPrefixUtil across the array elements.

- The immediately invoked function at the bottom:
  - It runs a perpetual loop that appears to scramble/index-shuffle the internal string array until a numeric check passes, effectively anti-tampering/anti-debugging setup for the obfuscated data.

In short:
- The code is heavily obfuscated. Its visible functionality is to decrypt and cache obfuscated strings and to compute the longest common prefix across a set of strings, using the decrypted data.

mbpp_0714.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.

It sums over all prime factors and returns the total count. Concretely, for each prime i dividing n with exponent total, it increments count for every k from 1 to total where k is added in triangular numbers (1, 3, 6, 10, ... as partial sums). After processing all primes, if a remaining factor n > 1 exists (a prime), it increments count once.

mbpp_0853.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find sum of odd factors of a number.

mbpp_0020.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: isWoodall function - detects Woodall numbers

Main goal: Determine whether a given integer x is a Woodall number (also known as Woodall primes context used here is a specific form). The function returns true for certain odd inputs that meet the defined condition, and false otherwise.

What it does:
- If x is even, returns false.
- If x equals 1, returns true.
- Sets m = x + 1 and p = 0, then repeatedly halves m while it is even, incrementing p.
- If at any point p equals the current m, returns true.
- If the loop finishes without p ever equaling m, returns false.

In short, it tests a particular relationship between x+1 and its powers of two to decide Woodall-related membership.

mbpp_0122.reference_description: Write a function to find n’th smart number.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming for Maximum Path Sum Average in an N x N Grid

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the maximum possible sum along a path from the top-left corner (0,0) to the bottom-right corner (N-1,N-1) in an N x N grid, using only moves right or down.
- Then return the average value of that path by dividing the total maximum sum by (2N - 1), which is the number of cells visited on such a path (N-1 rights + N-1 downs + 1 starting cell).

What the functions do:
- Initialize a 2D dp array to store the maximum sum reachable at each cell.
- Set dp[0][0] to cost[0][0].
- Fill the first row and first column with cumulative sums, since only one path exists to those cells.
- For each other cell, compute dp[i][j] as the maximum of the sums from the top or left neighbor, plus the current cell cost, effectively finding the best path to that cell.
- Return the value at dp[N-1][N-1] divided by (2N - 1), giving the average along the optimal path.

What the code does
- Main goal: Determine if there exists a subset of the given set of numbers that sums to a specified target value.

How it works
- isSubsetSum(set, n, sum) is a recursive function.
- Base cases:
  - If sum is 0, a subset with sum equal to the target is found; return true.
  - If no elements remain (n === 0) and sum is not 0, return false.
- Recursive step:
  - If the current (n-1)th element (set[n-1]) is greater than the remaining sum, exclude it and recurse on the remaining elements.
  - Otherwise, explore two possibilities: exclude the current element or include it (subtract its value from sum) and recurse.
- The function returns true if either path yields a subset summing to the target, otherwise false.

Short summary description:
<Summary_description>
A recursive function that checks whether any subset of the given set sums to the specified target value by exploring include/exclude choices for each element.

Summary_description:

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Shortest Common Supersequence Length Calculator (Recursive)

Main goal of the code:
- Computes the length of the shortest common supersequence (SCS) for two strings X and Y using a recursive approach.
- superSeq(X, Y, m, n) returns the length of the SCS for the prefixes X[0..m-1] and Y[0..n-1].

What the functions do:
- Base cases:
  - If m == 0, the SCS length is n (need all of Y).
  - If n == 0, the SCS length is m (need all of X).
- If the last characters match (X[m-1] === Y[n-1]), they contribute one character to the SCS, and the problem reduces to the prefixes (m-1, n-1).
- If the last characters differ, take one more character for the SCS and recursively compute the minimum between reducing m by 1 (skip a char from X) or reducing n by 1 (skip a char from Y). The result is 1 + min(superSeq(m-1, n), superSeq(m, n-1)).

Note: This is a pure recursive implementation without memoization, which can be inefficient for larger inputs due to overlapping subproblems.

mbpp_0828.reference_description: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.

mbpp_0657.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.

Goal: Compute the first (most significant) non-zero digit of n! (the factorial of n).

How it works:
- Multiplies numbers from 2 to n to form fact.
- After each multiplication, removes trailing zeros by dividing by 10 while fact ends with 0.
- Keeps only the integer part after each step.
- After the loop, reduces fact to its most significant digit by repeatedly dividing by 10 until a single digit remains.
- Returns that leading non-zero digit of n!.

mbpp_0225.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary Search-Based Minimum Finder in a Rotated Sorted Array

Main goal of the code:
- The function findMin locates and returns the minimum element in a rotated sorted array (assumed to be without duplicates) by using a modified binary search. It maintains a search window [low, high], compares mid with high to deduce which side contains the minimum, and narrows the range until low equals high, at which point arr[high] (the minimum) is returned.

Key behavior:
- If arr[mid] == arr[high], it reduces the high boundary by 1.
- If arr[mid] > arr[high], the minimum lies to the right of mid (low = mid + 1).
- If arr[mid] < arr[high], the minimum is at mid or to the left (high = mid).

The loop terminates when low == high, returning the smallest element.

mbpp_0605.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Purpose and behavior of the prime_num function

Main goal of the code:
- Determine whether a given number is prime, returning true if it is prime and false otherwise.

What the code does (summary):
- If num is less than 1, it returns false.
- For num >= 1, it iterates i from 2 up to floor(num/2) - 1, and checks divisibility.
- If num is divisible by any i, it returns false.
- If not divisible for the first tested i, it returns true immediately (early return).

Important issues:
- The loop and return logic are flawed. It only checks divisibility for i = 2 (due to the immediate return in the first iteration), so it wrongly classifies many composite numbers as prime.
- For num = 2 or 3, behavior is inconsistent with the intended primality test, and the condition should typically loop up to Math.floor(num / 2) inclusive or, more efficiently, up to Math.sqrt(num) and only return true after the loop completes without finding a divisor.
- The initial if condition should handle numbers <= 1 as non-prime, and the for-loop bounds should be corrected to properly test all necessary divisors.

mbpp_0627.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description: 
Goal: This function finds the first missing non-negative integer in a sorted array where the value at each index equals its index when no numbers are missing (i.e., array[i] == i for all i). It uses a binary search approach to locate the smallest index where the value differs from the index, which corresponds to the first missing number.

What it does:
- If start > end, returns end + 1 as the next missing candidate.
- If the value at the start index is not equal to the index (array[start] !== start), returns start as the first missing number.
- Computes mid and uses a binary search invariant:
  - If array[mid] == mid, the first missing number lies to the right; recurse on (mid + 1, end).
  - Otherwise, the first missing number is at or before mid; recurse on (start, mid).

Overall: It returns the smallest non-negative integer that is not present at its corresponding index in the sorted array.

- In short, it is designed to hide and then retrieve readable strings or code at runtime, typical of obfuscated payloads.

Key components and their roles:
- _0x6110(): Returns a long array of strings used as a dictionary for deobfuscation.
- _0x3963(...) and _0x4649(...): Two mirrored, self-contained deobfuscation functions (one named _0x3963 and the other similar) implementing:
  - A Base64-like decoding helper (_0x3d086 inside each) to decode a supplied key.
  - An RC4-like key scheduling and stream generation (_0x59d65f inside _0x3963) to decrypt input.
  - Caching objects (MlWUJs, scKtZN, etc.) to store previously decoded values for performance.
- _0x4649(_0x9bd6e9, _0xea7fb4): Public-facing function that takes an numeric index (after adjustment) and returns a decrypted string from the dictionary, using the per-function caches and the inner decryption function NIVxMm (or similar) the first time, then reusing cached results.
- divisibleByDigits(...): A small helper that, given two numbers, returns the list of numbers in that range divisible by at least one of the digits of the number, but it is not invoked in the provided snippet and may be part of the obfuscated logic.

Overall behavior:
- The code is an obfuscated loader that, when given an index, retrieves and decrypts a string from a concealed dictionary, using a combination of Base64 decoding and RC4-like decryption, with memoization to speed up repeated lookups. The structure and repeated patterns strongly suggest its purpose is to conceal strings or code and reconstruct them at runtime.

mbpp_0974.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.

Title: Minimized Path Sum in a Triangle

Starting from the bottom row, it initializes memo with that row, then iteratively updates memo[j] as A[i][j] plus the minimum of the two adjacent values from the row below (memo[j] and memo[j+1]). mbpp_0187.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given two sequences.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) Recursive Solver

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the length of the longest common subsequence between two sequences X and Y using a recursive approach.

What it does:
- longestCommonSubsequence(X, Y, m, n) takes two arrays/strings X and Y and indices m, n representing lengths considered from each.
- Base case: if either m or n is 0, there is no subsequence, so it returns 0.
- If the last characters (or elements) under consideration match (X[m-1] === Y[n-1]), it counts that match and recurses on the remaining prefixes (m-1, n-1) adding 1.
- If they don’t match, it explores two possibilities: skip a character in X (m-1, n) or skip a character in Y (m, n-1), and returns the maximum of the two results, effectively choosing the longer subsequence.

Note:
- This is a classic recursive solution to the LCS problem with exponential time complexity due to overlapping subproblems (no memoization).

  - It defines a countReversePairs function that, given an array of strings (or subarrays), counts the number of pairs where two identical elements appear in different positions, effectively computing the number of reverse-equal pairs in a 2D array-like structure.
  - It initializes a self-contained decoding environment and a scrambling/unscrambling bootstrap that reorders an array until a condition is satisfied (typical of anti-tookit obfuscation).

In summary, the code is primarily an obfuscated implementation that:

mbpp_0025.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Summary of the findProduct function

Main goal of the code:
- To compute a product of certain distinct values in a given array after sorting, effectively multiplying each unique value exactly once while skipping duplicates and handling wrap-around comparison.

What the code does:
- Sorts the array in ascending order.
- Initializes a product variable to 1.
- Iterates over the first n elements of the sorted array.
- For each element, compares it to the previous element (with a wrap-around to the last element for i = 0).
- If the current value is different from the previous value, multiplies the product by the current value; otherwise, skips it.
- Returns the final product.

Notes and edge cases:
- Duplicates are ignored: only the first occurrence of each distinct value in the sorted array contributes to the product.
- The wrap-around comparison for i = 0 uses arr[n - 1], which means the first element is compared to the last element to determine duplication, which can lead to unusual behavior if the array starts with a value equal to the last value.
- If the array contains zeros, the product becomes zero if any distinct value is zero.
- If all elements are the same, the product remains 1 (no distinct values multiplied).

mbpp_0556.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the pairs with xor as an odd number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to count the pairs with xor as an odd number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Odd XOR Pair Counter

Main goal: The code counts the number of distinct pairs (i, j) with i < j in array A of length N such that the bitwise XOR of A[i] and A[j] is odd. It returns the total count of such pairs.

How it works:
- Initialize oddPair to 0.
- Use a double loop to examine every unordered pair (i, j) where i < j.
- For each pair, compute (A[i] ^ A[j]) and check if the result is odd (i.e., the least significant bit is 1, meaning ((A[i] ^ A[j]) % 2) !== 0).
- If the XOR is odd, increment oddPair.
- Return oddPair after examining all pairs.

In effect, the code counts pairs of numbers with differing parity (one even, one odd), since XOR of even and odd is odd.

Title: Obfuscated JavaScript Decoder/Initializer

Main goal of the code:
- The snippet is an obfuscated JavaScript IIFE (immediately invoked function expression) that sets up and executes a small decoding/string-decrypting utility. It defines several hidden helpers to:
  - Decode Base64-like strings with a custom cache (_0xEhbnSj, _0xUkTGfZ, etc.).
  - Decrypt or transform strings via a custom RC4-like routine.
  - Count certain character positions in strings (countCharPosition).
- The overall effect is to hide the real strings and logic behind multiple indirections and runtime decoding, likely to reconstruct and run some payload or configuration without exposing it in plain text.

Key components and their roles:
- _0x3313 and _0x2a4a / _0x15df: Functions that map numeric indices to encoded strings from an internal array, with lazy decoding and caching. They serve as string obfuscation lookups.

- The main IIFE repeatedly attempts to compute a numeric expression and compare it to a target (0xc55e5). If mismatch, it rotates the internal string array to try another alignment. This is a common anti-topology/anti-tamper technique used in obfuscated payloads.
- countCharPosition: Utility that counts the number of characters in a string that are uppercase or lowercase ASCII letters, based on the computed string contents.

Overall, the code’s primary purpose is to conceal and then reconstruct/execute hidden strings or payloads at runtime, typically seen in obfuscated or malicious code. It hides its true actions behind multiple layers of indirection and dynamic decoding.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Check for a Perfect Square

Main goal: Determine whether a given positive integer n is a perfect square by iterating through possible divisors and verifying if a pair of equal factors multiply to n.

What it does:
- Iterates i from 1 upward while i*i <= n.
- For each i, checks if i divides n and if n / i equals i.
- If such i is found, returns true (n is a perfect square).
- If no such i is found after the loop, returns false.

Note: The function uses divisor comparison instead of directly computing a square root and comparing.

mbpp_0103.reference_description: Write a function to find eulerian number a(n, m).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find eulerian number a(n, m).
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Eulerian Number Computation

Main goal of the code:
- This function eulerianNum(n, m) computes the Eulerian number A(n, m), which counts the number of permutations of n elements with exactly m ascents (positions i where p(i) < p(i+1)).
- It uses the standard recurrence: A(n, m) = (n − m) * A(n − 1, m − 1) + (m + 1) * A(n − 1, m), with base cases:
  - If m >= n or n === 0, A(n, m) = 0
  - If m === 0, A(n, 0) = 1

What the functions do:
- Validate inputs and handle edge cases.
- Recursively compute the Eulerian numbers via the recurrence relation.

Title: Summary of doesContainB Function

Main goal of the code:
- Determines whether the value b is “contained” relative to a and c, returning true if b equals a or if the difference (b - a) is a nonzero multiple of c with the same sign as c.

What the function does:
- If a === b, it returns true.
- Otherwise, it checks two conditions: (b - a) * c > 0 ensures b - a and c have the same sign (nonzero step in the intended direction), and (b - a) % c === 0 ensures (b - a) is a multiple of c. If both are true, it returns true.
- If neither condition holds, it returns false.

mbpp_0148.reference_description: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Compute the sum of digits of a number N by splitting it into two parts to minimize or structure the digit-sum calculation.

Functions:
- sumDigitsSingle(x): Returns the sum of the decimal digits of x by iterating through each digit (x % 10) and reducing x (x = floor(x/10)).
- closest(x): Builds the largest number composed of all 9s that is less than or equal to x (e.g., for x = 572 -> 499). It starts with 0 and appends 9s while (ans * 10 + 9) <= x.
- sumDigitsTwoParts(N): Splits N into A and N - A, where A is the number consisting of all 9s with the same length constraints as N, via closest(N). It then returns sumDigitsSingle(A) + sumDigitsSingle(N - A), effectively computing the total digit sum by summing the digit sums of the two parts.

Overall, the code computes the sum of the digits of N by partitioning N into two parts (A with trailing 9s and the remainder) and summing their digit sums.

This effectively counts the number of substrings ending at i whose digit-sum equals the number of characters in the substring, i.e., substrings where sum(substring) = length(substring). The initial mp[0] = 1 accounts for substrings starting at index 0. In short, it uses prefix sums and a frequency map to count substrings with a specific relationship between total digit sum and substring length.

Returns the total sum of divisors (excluding n itself, since start is 1 and n is only added as pair when i <= sqrt(n)).
- areEquivalent(num1, num2): Returns true if divSum(num1) equals divSum(num2); i.e., the two numbers have the same sum of divisors.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Adjacency Expansion Generator in JavaScript

Main goal: Generate all combinations of adjacent integer offsets for a given list of numbers by recursively constructing every possible set where each element is replaced by a value within -1, 0, or +1 of its original value.

What the code does:
- adjac(ele, sub = []) recursively processes an array ele.
  - If ele is empty, it returns the accumulated sub as a single combination: [sub].
  - Otherwise, it iterates j from ele[0]-1 to ele[0]+1, and for each j, recursively calls adjac on the remaining elements (ele.slice(1)) with the current choice appended to sub (sub.concat(j)).
  - It concatenates all results from these recursive calls, effectively exploring all 3^n combinations for an input of length n.
- getCoordinates(testTup) is a thin wrapper that calls adjac(testTup) to produce the same set of combinations.

In short, given a tuple of integers, the code generates all possible tuples where each original element is replaced by one of its three neighboring integers (original-1, original, original+1).

At each step, it decides either to skip A[i] (carrying lookUp[i-1]) or take A[i] (adding A[i] to lookUp[i-2]), and ensures the result is at least A[i] itself. The final result is lookUp[n-1].

mbpp_0707.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the total set bits from 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to count the total set bits from 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description: 
Goal: The function countSetBits(n) computes the total number of set bits (1s) in the binary representations of all integers from 0 to n inclusive.

What it does:
- It first increments n by 1 to work with a half-open range.
- It iterates over powers of two (2, 4, 8, ...) to accumulate the count of 1s contributed by each bit position across all numbers in [0, n-1].
- For each bit position corresponding to powerOf2, it calculates how many complete blocks of that bit occur (totalPairs) and adds the number of set bits contributed by full pairs. If there is a partial block (totalPairs is odd), it adds the remainder n % powerOf2 to cnt.
- The loop doubles powerOf2 each iteration, effectively processing each bit position from least significant upwards.
- Finally, it returns cnt, the total count of set bits in all numbers from 0 to the original n (inclusive).

mbpp_0169.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the nth pell number.

- Initialization and runtime decoding: The code runs an IIFE that shuffles an array to further obfuscate execution flow, and the capitalizer uses the decoders to dynamically assemble results.

Overall, the code’s purpose is to obfuscate string literals and functionality, provide a runtime string-decode mechanism with caching, and offer a small text-capitalization utility that relies on those obfuscated strings.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Equilibrium Index Finder in an Array

Main goal: The code finds the index in an array where the sum of elements to the left equals the sum of elements to the right (the equilibrium index). It returns the first such index, or -1 if none exists.

What it does:
- Computes totalSum as the sum of all elements.
- Iterates through the array, updating totalSum to exclude the current element (so totalSum becomes the right-side sum).
- Compares leftSum (sum of elements left of current index) with totalSum (sum of elements to the right).
- If they are equal, returns the current index.
- Otherwise, adds the current element to leftSum and continues.
- If no equilibrium index is found, returns -1.

Title: Maximum Frequency Finder in an Array

Main goal: The code identifies the value in list1 that occurs most frequently (the mode) and returns that value. If multiple values share the maximum frequency, it returns the one encountered first during iteration.

What it does:
- Initializes maxVal to track the highest occurrence count and result to hold the current most frequent value.

- Counts occurrences of i in the entire list via list1.filter(item => item === i).length.

Note: This approach is O(n^2) due to the inner filter in each iteration and may be inefficient for large lists.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary Search Insertion Point (Right Insertion)

Main goal: Find the index where a value x would be inserted into a sorted ascending array a to keep it sorted, choosing the position after any existing equal elements (i.e., the rightmost insertion point).

What it does:
- rightInsertion(a, x) performs a binary search on the sorted array a.
- It returns the smallest index lo such that x < a[lo] is true; equivalently, the position to insert x so that all elements <= x are to the left.
- If x is greater than or equal to all elements, it returns a.length (insertion at the end).
- It handles duplicates by placing x after existing equal elements (rightmost insertion).

Summary_description:

The result is the maximum of these options, stored in dp[i]. The function returns dp[n].

It assumes A is non-decreasing and uses the invariant that, for a correct index i, A[i] should equal i. If A[mid] equals mid, it searches the right half to find a larger missing value; if A[mid] does not equal mid, it searches the left half for the first mismatch.

Summary:

- If leftElement > rightElement, it returns leftElement as the smallest missing index.
- If A[mid] == mid, continue in the right half; otherwise, search the left half.

Main goal: The function highestPowerOf2(n) finds and returns the largest power of 2 that is less than or equal to the given integer n. If no such power exists (e.g., n <= 0), it returns 0.

How it works:
- It iterates from i = n down to 1.
- For each i, it checks if i is a power of 2 using the bit trick (i & (i - 1)) === 0.
- Once it finds the first such i (the largest power of 2 ≤ n), it assigns res = i and exits the loop, returning res.

Title: Code Analysis of solve(a, n)

Main goal of the code:
- The function solve(a, n) checks a property of the array a of length n. It iterates j from 1 to n-1, maintaining a running maximum mx (initialized to -Infinity). If at any point mx is greater than a[j], the function immediately returns false. After the check, mx is updated to the maximum of its current value and a[j - 1]. If the loop completes without returning false, the function returns true. In short, it returns true if, for every position j from 1 to n-1, the maximum value seen among a[0..j-1] is not greater than a[j]; equivalently, a[j] is at least as large as the maximum of all previous elements up to j-1.

mbpp_0325.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is equal to a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is equal to a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum Number of Perfect Squares Summing to n

Main goal: This code computes the least number of perfect square numbers that sum to n (the minimum count of squares that add up to n).

Summary description:
- getMinSquares(n) returns the smallest number of perfect square terms whose sum equals n.
- Base case: if n <= 3, the minimum count is n itself (since 1^2 = 1, 2^2 = 4 etc., but for small n, n copies of 1 suffice).
- Recursive step: for each x from 1 up to floor(sqrt(n)), it considers using x^2 as part of the sum and recursively solves for n - x^2, plus one for the current square.
- Chooses the minimum over all possible first squares, effectively performing a depth-first search with memoization not present (so exponential without caching in practice).

mbpp_0402.reference_description: Write a function to compute the value of ncr%p.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to compute the value of ncr%p.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Modular Binomial Coefficient Calculator (nCr mod p)

Main goal: Compute the value of r choose n modulo a prime p using a space-efficient dynamic programming approach.

What the code does:
- It initializes a 1D array C of length r+1 with zeros, and sets C[0] = 1.
- It iterates i from 1 to n. For each i, it updates C from j = min(i, r) down to 1:
  - C[j] = (C[j] + C[j - 1]) mod p
- This update uses the standard Pascal triangle relation to accumulate binomial coefficients C(i, j) modulo p, reusing the same array.
- After processing all i, C[r] holds the value of nCr modulo p, which is returned.

Note: The function effectively computes n choose r modulo p, assuming p is a modulus (often a prime), using an in-place dynamic programming approach with O(r) extra space and O(nr) time.

Main goal: The function scans a list of words to find the first pair where two consecutive tokens start with the letter P and are separated by a non-word character; it then returns the two matched tokens as an array.

What it does:
- Iterates over the input array "words".
- For each word w, it tries to match the pattern /^(P\w+)\W(P\w+)/ against the entire string.
  - This pattern captures two groups:
    - m[1]: a token starting with 'P' followed by one or more word characters.
    - m[2]: another token starting with 'P' followed by one or more word characters.
  - The \W in between requires a non-word character between the two P-words.
- If a match is found, it returns an array [m[1], m[2]] containing the two P-words.
- If no such pair exists in any element, the function returns undefined.

mbpp_0545.reference_description: Write a javascript function to toggle only first and last bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to toggle only first and last bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Bitwise Masking Functions to Compute and Toggle Pattern Bits

Main goal of the code:
- The code defines two functions that manipulate bits of a 32-bit integer to generate a specific mask and to toggle certain bits based on that mask.

Functions:
- takeLAndFSetBits(n):
  - Creates a progressively larger bitmask by propagating set bits to the right: n |= n>>1, n|=n>>2, etc.
  - This results in n having a run of 1s from the most significant set bit down to bit 0 (i.e., a contiguous block of 1s up to the highest 1-bit).
  - Returns ((n + 1) >> 1) + 1, which effectively derives a particular offset-related value from that mask (roughly related to the position of the highest set bit and the mask width).

- toggleFAndLBits(n):
  - If n is 1, returns 0.
  - Otherwise, returns n XOR takeLAndFSetBits(n).
  - This toggles bits of n using the mask produced by takeLAndFSetBits(n), effectively flipping the bits in the region defined by that mask.

Overall, the code computes a specific bitmask from n and then uses it to flip (XOR) bits of n, with a special-case handling for n === 1.

mbpp_0735.reference_description: Write a javascript function to toggle bits of the number except the first and the last bit.

Functions:
- setMiddleBits(n): Propagates set bits to fill consecutive lower bits from the highest set bit downward, through a sequence of OR-shift operations, then returns a value that isolates a specific middle-bit region by shifting right and xoring with 1.
- toggleMiddleBits(n): If n is 1, returns 1; otherwise, returns n XOR setMiddleBits(n), effectively toggling the bits in the middle region identified by setMiddleBits(n).

Overall: It appears to generate a mask representing a central block of bits and then flips those bits in n, with a special case for n == 1. The exact middle-bit region corresponds to the propagated pattern produced by the successive n |= n >> k operations.

What the code does:

  - Updates deciNum by dividing by 8 (integer division) to process the next digit.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the maximum sum such that no two chosen numbers are adjacent for the given rectangular grid of dimension 2 x n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Sum of Non-Adjacent Elements in a 2-Row Grid

Main goal of the code:
- This function computes the maximum possible sum by selecting one element from each column of a 2-row grid, with the constraint that no two chosen elements are in adjacent columns. It effectively finds the best alternating choices across the two rows for n columns.

What it does:
- grid is a 2xN matrix (two rows, n columns).
- It uses a dynamic programming approach with two running values:
  - incl: the maximum sum ending at the current column when choosing an element from the same column (i.e., including the column’s chosen value).
  - excl: the maximum sum ending at the current column when not choosing any element from the current column (or effectively the best sum up to previous column with the constraint).
- Initialization uses the first column: incl = max(grid[0][0], grid[1][0]); excl = 0.
- For each subsequent column i (1 to n-1):
  - exclNew is the best sum so far without using column i (max of previous incl and excl).
  - incl is updated to exclude conflicts by adding the best value from column i (max(grid[0][i], grid[1][i])) to excl.
  - excl is updated to exclNew.
- The result is the maximum of excl and incl after processing all columns.

In short, the code selects one value per column from the two rows, ensuring no two chosen values are in adjacent columns, to maximize the total sum.

Title: Profit Amount Calculator

Main goal: To compute the profit as the difference between actualCost and saleAmount if a profit is possible; it returns the profit amount when actualCost is greater than saleAmount, otherwise it returns null.
